{
  "signals_observed": [
    "Alert date: 2025-05-07; merchant_id: 75.",
    "Trigger B: AUP-06.1 breach: 30d chargeback rate 7.3% (3 disputes / 41 orders).",
    "cb_rate_30d: 0.07317073170731707; disputes_30d: 3; orders_30d: 41.",
    "gmv_30d: 673648 cents; base_gmv: 1325520 cents over base_days: 90.",
    "volume_z: 2.9417420270727606; base_orders: 78.",
    "new_gmv_share: 0.12162138089922334; new_gmv_30d: 81930 cents.",
    "ticket_drift: 0.9668464028475159.",
    "refunds_30d: 0; refund_rate_30d: 0.0; base_refunds: 0; base_refund_rate: 0.0.",
    "cum_orders: 469; days_since_first_order: 491; merchant_age_days: 1014."
  ],
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "kind": "bustout",
      "likelihood": "med",
      "reasoning": "The chargeback breach and volume_z of 2.9417420270727606 warrant investigation. Three disputes provide limited evidence, and the metrics do not establish non-delivery, thin buyer accounts or coordinated purchasing."
    },
    {
      "kind": "marketing_push",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "A campaign could explain increased order volume, but no campaign evidence is supplied. Verified campaign timing and completed deliveries would support this explanation; campaign activity alone would not explain the disputes."
    },
    {
      "kind": "seasonal_spike",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "Seasonal demand could explain the volume increase, but merchant category and comparable seasonal history are unavailable. Matching seasonal patterns and verified fulfillment would strengthen this hypothesis."
    },
    {
      "kind": "data_issue",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "Missing orders, duplicate disputes or incomplete refund ingestion could distort the reported rates. No pipeline failure is observed, so this remains a hypothesis requiring reconciliation."
    }
  ],
  "recommended_action": "reserve",
  "evidence_gaps": [
    "Review the three dispute records: confirm unique cases, linked orders, reasons and current status. Non-delivery complaints would strengthen concern; invalid or duplicated records would weaken the alert.",
    "Check fulfillment and delivery evidence for disputed orders and a small sample of recent orders; corroborate receipt with buyers where records are ambiguous. Widespread failed delivery would support escalation.",
    "Reconcile refund requests, pending refunds and completed refunds against source records. Zero recorded refunds does not establish successful fulfillment.",
    "Request campaign dates, promotion records and seasonal sales comparisons. A matching sales increase with verified fulfillment would support a benign explanation.",
    "Reconcile the 41 orders and three disputes with source systems and check ingestion completeness, deduplication and window assignment.",
    "Inspect buyer-account history and links among recent orders to determine whether the volume increase involves thin or coordinated accounts; new_gmv_share alone cannot establish this."
  ],
  "memo_markdown": "As of May 7, merchant 75 breached the reported AUP-06.1 chargeback threshold: three disputes across 41 trailing-30-day orders (7.3%). Volume_z is 2.94, new GMV share is 12.16%, and ticket_drift is 0.967. No refunds are recorded. These observations warrant review but do not establish bust-out or non-delivery.\n\nRecommend a proportionate payout reserve while the human owner reviews the evidence. Prioritize the three dispute files, delivery confirmation and refund reconciliation, then verify campaign timing and source-data completeness. Marketing or seasonal demand could explain the volume increase if fulfillment is sound.\n\nConfirmed non-delivery across recent orders, especially with coordinated thin buyers, would strengthen bust-out concerns and support pausing settlement pending review. Verified deliveries, resolved or invalid disputes, or a corrected data error would weaken the alert and support releasing the reserve and monitoring. Offboarding requires corroborated bust-out evidence."
}
